title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (made explicit on the next page): X/S is a smooth relative curve in characteristic 0. P is a P^1-bundle over X with a section σ. Equivalently (P,σ) is given by an extension 0→Ω→E→O→0 with Ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. Ŝ is the completed local ring of P along σ: an adic, O_X-augmented algebra with ideal J and J/J^2 ≅ Ω (the normal bundle of σ is the tangent bundle, up to dualisation conventions). A connection c on P (relative to S) induces a connection ĉ on Ŝ. It respects the algebra structure but not the augmentation, since σ need not be horizontal; this is the transversality condition of an indigenous bundle / oper. On the other side, 𝒫 is an abstract adic augmented O_X-algebra with a connection C_P. The model is the principal-parts algebra P^∞_{X/S}, the formal neighbourhood of the diagonal, with its canonical (Grothendieck) connection.

The problem: find the triples (P,σ,c) together with isomorphisms of augmented algebras v: 𝒫 → Ŝ such that v(C_P) is of the form ĉ, i.e. comes from a genuine connection on P.

The page's argument:
(1) An isomorphism to order 2, 𝒫/J^3 ≅ Ŝ/Ĵ^3, already determines the extension 0→Ω→E→O→0, hence (P,σ) up to unique isomorphism.
(2) Fix such an isomorphism. Transport C_P to a connection C on Ŝ. Let G be the group of automorphisms of Ŝ that are the identity to order 2. One seeks g ∈ G with g·C of the form ĉ.
(3) If g_0 is one solution, with g_0 C = ĉ_0, every other solution is g = h g_0. The condition is that h·ĉ_0 is again of the form ĉ', i.e. h lies in the subgroup of G preserving 'algebraic' connections, written G(c). The solution set is therefore a torsor under that subgroup and is described as a coset space (written G/G_0).

The next page states the outcome as a theorem: any order-3 isomorphism extending the order-2 one extends uniquely to a full isomorphism û with û(C) of the form ĉ. So a projective connection / indigenous bundle is the same as a 3-jet of a formal uniformising identification. This is the algebraic, relative and formal version of the classical fact that a projective structure is determined by third-order data (the Schwarzian derivative), with P^1-bundle plus section plus transverse connection as the global object. The aim is 'uniformisation' in families over a base S.
errors: Notation for the residual freedom is unstable. h is said to lie in G, then G(c), and the solution set is identified with 'G/G_0'. As written this is not consistent: the solution set should be a torsor (coset) under the stabiliser-type subgroup G(c), not obviously the quotient G/G_0. The next page makes this precise via the order-3 statement.
Draft relation 'gC = k Ĉ_0, (h∈G_0), hence (k^{-1}g)C = Ĉ_0' mixes the letters h and k. It is a working note, not an error of substance.
The page ends mid-sentence ('ainsi que pour la catégorie de ...').

ideas.what: Encoding a projective connection on a relative curve as a P^1-bundle with a section σ and a connection transverse to σ (normal bundle of σ ≅ tangent bundle).
Formal completion of P along σ as an adic augmented O_X-algebra with connection, compared with the principal-parts algebra P^∞_{X/S} and its canonical connection.
ideas.modern_name: formal neighbourhood of the diagonal / Grothendieck connection on jets; formal developing map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (principal parts and stratifications in EGA IV, crystals); Berthelot
ideas.where_published: EGA IV §16 (principal parts); 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968) for stratifications

ideas.what: Order-2 jet data determines (P,σ) via the extension 0→Ω→E→O→0; order-3 data then determines the full formal isomorphism uniquely.
ideas.modern_name: projective structure determined by 3-jets / Schwarzian derivative; jet-level rigidity of opers
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); algebraic treatments by Deligne (1970) and later the oper literature

ideas.what: Gauge-group argument: the automorphisms of Ŝ that are the identity to order 2 act on connections; the solutions form a torsor under the subgroup preserving connections of 'algebraic' form.
ideas.modern_name: torsor / stabiliser argument in jet groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up projective connections / indigenous bundles relatively over an arbitrary base S, through formal geometry: the completion of a P^1-bundle along a transverse section, matched with principal parts carrying their Grothendieck connection. This links his crystalline / principal-parts machinery to uniformisation in families, which is essentially the oper / indigenous-bundle formalism later developed independently.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a jet-theoretic, base-change-friendly characterisation of opers via comparison of adic algebras with connection. It is of historical interest for the prehistory of Mochizuki's p-adic uniformisation and of Beilinson–Drinfeld opers, if the note predates them.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is likely a formulation as an equivalence of categories (or groupoids) between projective connections and suitable jet data. It is standard in spirit today, but the note shows Grothendieck intended it.

deep.surprise_reason: The page shows Grothendieck independently developing an algebraic, relative and formal-geometric version of indigenous bundles / opers, with the order-2 / order-3 jet determination. The mathematics itself is classical in content (Gunning, Schwarzian; later Deligne, Beilinson–Drinfeld, Mochizuki). The interest is mainly historical and in the formal-algebra viewpoint, not a new result.
